premises.text: The vision system detects berries, decides which to pick, and locates them on the plant
premises.evidence_span: Our vision system detects the berries in that image, decides which to pick, figures out the position of that berry

premises.text: A unique patented gripper closes with defined force so it can grab produce of different sizes without crushing or dropping it
premises.evidence_span: We close the fingers with a defined amount of force, allowing us to grab objects of different sizes without crushing or dropping them.

premises.text: The self-contained system operates continuously in real field conditions with all compute on board
premises.evidence_span: Our system does all this in real time while hanging off the back of a tractor and moving continuously over real strawberry fields.

premises.text: Year-round strawberry harvest is a more valuable target than the low-value or seasonal tasks competitors chose
premises.evidence_span: some startups target low-value activities like weeding, only worth $1,000 to $2,000 per acre, or they harvest fruits like apples, where they're only needed a few months a year

premises.text: Deployment requires no change in the growing process
premises.evidence_span: We don't require any change in growing process, providing a smooth path for deployment.

premises.text: Growers pay 23 cents per pound for a full picking service, slightly less than their current spend
premises.evidence_span: growers will pay us 23 cents per pound. This is slightly less than the current spend.

value.text: Growers outsource strawberry harvest to robots at slightly below their current picking cost
value.evidence_span: We pick strawberries, and growers will pay us 23 cents per pound.

secondary_value.text: Saving the world's food production system by automating work people do not want to do
secondary_value.evidence_span: saving the world's food production system by automating the work people don't want to do

causal_links.evidence_span: it plans a path to grab it, and our software commands the robot arm to move the gripper to the berry
it operates all day, every day, for months and years on end
Traptic focuses on year-round strawberry harvest.

notes: Field robustness and on-board compute merged into one self-contained-operation premise (both describe operating the same machine in situ). Grower partnerships and next-year commercial deployment read as traction and excluded. Master-plan revenue ladder and 'future of robotics is outdoors' treated as vision framing, uncoded per v1.3.2 clarification 4; the food-production claim recorded as a secondary value criterion. Two domains: one machine module, one market-and-service module.
